title: Asian Travelers Still Plan Trips Despite Rising Costs
paragraphs: Rising costs around the world have changed the way many people travel. Some are taking fewer vacations, while others are choosing to travel around their own country instead.
But others aren't letting rising costs stop them. In fact, many Asian travelers still plan to travel before the year ends.
A survey done by travel company Klook asked people in 10 Asian countries about traveling. All the participants had traveled in the first six months of 2026.
The results showed that, for many travelers, travel confidence is a bit higher for the second half of 2026, compared with the first.
And although travel is becoming more expensive, 95% of participants said they are still interested in traveling to another country.
The survey included just over 1,000 travelers from Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, South Korea, Hong Kong, Taiwan and India.

Travelers in Taiwan showed the highest travel confidence — 86% said they were as willing, or more willing, to travel in the second half of the year as they had been in the first. This was 14 percentage points above the average for all 10 countries.
Many participants said they planned to keep traveling, but added that they would have to budget more carefully.
Many said they'd do this by planning better, such as booking early or looking for travel deals.
And with overcrowding becoming a big problem in many parts of the world, many people are looking for quieter places to travel to.
Just under two-thirds of participants said overcrowding has made them want to visit lesser-known places when they travel. And 20% said they have stopped going to popular tourist destinations.
Many participants said they had recently taken a side trip to a lesser-known destination — and some said it was one of the best parts of their trip!
